title: Scope-isolated preflight and trace relocation
objective: Bind the integrity preflight and its verification to the resolved scope, move trace out of the scope-discovery tree, and gate both against regression.

phases.title: Scope-isolated preflight
phases.objective: Make all four startup surfaces resolve the scope first and keep every integrity operation and its verification bound to that scope.

tasks.title: Resolve scope before integrity prepare in the three routers
tasks.description: Reorder the startup steps in commands/forge.md, internal/skills/sprint-forge/SKILL.md and agents/orchestrator.md so the target scope is resolved before repair integrity prepare runs, and pass --kyro-scope to it. Stop when no single scope can be resolved instead of running an unscoped preflight.
tasks.context: prepareIntegrityPlan (src/cli/repair/integrity-plan.ts) scans every registered scope, every archive scope and every scope folder when kyroScope is null, so an unscoped preflight made one broken scope block all routing.
acceptance_criteria: All three routers resolve the scope before invoking repair integrity prepare.
All three routers pass --kyro-scope to repair integrity prepare.
An unresolvable or ambiguous scope stops and asks instead of running an unscoped preflight.

evidence.summary: Reordered startup in the three routers so the scope resolves before repair integrity prepare, which now always receives --kyro-scope; an unresolvable scope stops and asks instead of running an unscoped preflight.
validation: check:blast-radius-isolation asserts scope resolution precedes prepare in all three routers and that no invocation omits --kyro-scope
Sandbox: repair integrity prepare --kyro-scope demo --json returns findings=[] blockers=[] with an irreconcilable sibling scope present
npm run check passes end to end (exit 0)

checked_criteria: All three routers resolve the scope before invoking repair integrity prepare.
All three routers pass --kyro-scope to repair integrity prepare.
An unresolvable or ambiguous scope stops and asks instead of running an unscoped preflight.

tasks.title: Keep recover mode scoped through apply and verification
tasks.description: Pass --kyro-scope to repair integrity prepare, repair integrity apply and the post-repair doctor --artifacts in recover mode, so a successful scoped repair is not undone by an unrelated scope's failure at verification time.
tasks.context: doctor --artifacts falls back to auditing every scope when --kyro-scope is absent (resolveScopeNames in src/cli/commands/artifact-doctor.ts).
acceptance_criteria: Recover mode passes --kyro-scope to prepare, apply and the post-repair doctor.
The mode states why the flag must never be dropped.

evidence.summary: Recover mode now passes --kyro-scope to repair integrity prepare, to repair integrity apply, and to the post-repair doctor --artifacts, and states why the flag must never be dropped.
validation: Confirmed in src/cli/commands/artifact-doctor.ts resolveScopeNames that doctor --artifacts audits every scope when --kyro-scope is absent
check:blast-radius-isolation asserts recover.md never invokes prepare/apply/doctor --artifacts without --kyro-scope
Sandbox: doctor --artifacts --kyro-scope demo exits 0 with an irreconcilable sibling scope present

checked_criteria: Recover mode passes --kyro-scope to prepare, apply and the post-repair doctor.
The mode states why the flag must never be dropped.

phases.title: Trace relocation and read compatibility
phases.objective: Move trace writes out of scopes/, keep previously recorded history readable in chronological order, and stop discovery from seeing leftover trace-only directories.

tasks.title: Write trace as a sibling of scopes/
tasks.description: Point traceDir at KYRO_PROJECT_ROOT/trace/{scope} instead of ARTIFACT_ROOT/{scope}/trace, and update the check scripts and docs that hardcode the previous location.
tasks.context: emitTraceEvent creates the trace directory for any scope string, and listScopeFolders treats every directory under scopes/ as a scope, so a trace write for a name without sprint.json produced a directory classified as an invalid scope.
acceptance_criteria: Trace events are written under .agents/kyro/trace/{scope}/.
No trace write creates a directory under .agents/kyro/scopes/.
Check scripts and docs reference the new location.

evidence.summary: traceDir now returns KYRO_PROJECT_ROOT/trace/{scope}, a sibling of scopes/ rather than a child, and the four check scripts plus two docs that hardcoded the previous location were updated.
validation: Sandbox close-sprint wrote .agents/kyro/trace/demo/events.ndjson and created nothing new under .agents/kyro/scopes/
check:trace, check:guardrails, check:maker-checker and check:status pass against the new location
check:blast-radius-isolation asserts no trace write creates a scope-like directory

checked_criteria: Trace events are written under .agents/kyro/trace/{scope}/.
No trace write creates a directory under .agents/kyro/scopes/.
Check scripts and docs reference the new location.

tasks.title: Merge previous-location trace history chronologically
tasks.description: Read both the current and the previous trace locations, merge them by timestamp with a stable tie-break, apply tail after merging, and make trace --clear remove both files.
tasks.context: Concatenating previous-location events before current ones assumes the previous path never grows again. A rollback or a mixed-version runtime breaks that assumption and would let --tail hide genuinely newer events.
acceptance_criteria: History at the previous location remains visible through kyro trace.
Merged output is ordered by timestamp regardless of which file an event came from.
Equal timestamps produce a stable, reproducible order.
tail is applied after the merge, so it keeps the newest events.
trace --clear removes both the current and the previous file.

evidence.summary: readTrace reads both locations and merges them by timestamp with a stable tie-break (previous location first, then original line index), applying tail after the merge; trace --clear removes both files. An earlier concatenation-based version was corrected after review showed it mis-ordered a rollback or mixed-runtime write.
validation: Verified against this repo's real history: 31 pre-move events for integrity-recovery remain readable via kyro trace
check:blast-radius-isolation asserts timestamp ordering when the previous location holds the newest event, and that --tail 1 keeps it
check:blast-radius-isolation asserts identical timestamps render the same stable order across repeated reads
Falsification: reverting the merge to plain concatenation makes the new assertions fail, so the gate is load-bearing

checked_criteria: History at the previous location remains visible through kyro trace.
Merged output is ordered by timestamp regardless of which file an event came from.
Equal timestamps produce a stable, reproducible order.
tail is applied after the merge, so it keeps the newest events.
trace --clear removes both the current and the previous file.

tasks.title: Ignore leftover trace-only directories in scope discovery
tasks.description: Make listScopeFolders skip any directory under scopes/ whose only entry is a trace folder, so installs upgraded from the previous layout stop carrying phantom scopes.
tasks.context: classifyOne marks an on-disk directory with no valid sprint.json as IRRECONCILABLE, which is a hard blocker.
acceptance_criteria: A directory containing only a trace folder is never reported as a scope.
A real scope directory is still discovered.

evidence.summary: listScopeFolders now skips any directory under scopes/ whose only entry is a trace folder, so installs upgraded from the previous layout stop surfacing phantom scopes as IRRECONCILABLE blockers.
validation: Sandbox: a scopes/ghost/trace-only directory no longer appears in repair integrity prepare --json output
check:blast-radius-isolation asserts a trace-only leftover is never discovered as a scope
check:scope-remediation (716 assertions) and check:repair-integrity (90 assertions) still pass, so real scope discovery is unaffected

checked_criteria: A directory containing only a trace folder is never reported as a scope.
A real scope directory is still discovered.

phases.title: Regression gate
phases.objective: Prove the isolation holds end to end and fail the build if any startup surface reintroduces a global preflight.

tasks.title: Add the blast-radius isolation gate
tasks.description: Add a portable check that statically asserts all four startup surfaces keep --kyro-scope and keep scope resolution ahead of prepare, and functionally asserts healthy/broken sibling isolation, preserved global scanning, phantom-scope suppression and trace merge ordering. Wire it into npm run check.
tasks.context: The contract lives in four separate Markdown assets that must stay in agreement; nothing previously failed when one of them drifted back to a global call.
acceptance_criteria: The gate fails when a startup surface drops --kyro-scope.
The gate fails when trace merge is not chronological.
The gate runs inside npm run check.
A healthy scope closes while an unrelated scope is irreconcilable.
An explicit global scan still reports the broken scope.

evidence.summary: Added scripts/check-blast-radius-isolation.mjs and wired it into npm run check. It combines static guards over the four startup surfaces with functional sandbox cases for sibling isolation, preserved global scanning, phantom-scope suppression and trace merge ordering.
validation: Falsification 1: dropping --kyro-scope from commands/forge.md makes the gate fail and name the file; restoring it makes it pass
Falsification 2: reverting the trace merge to concatenation makes the ordering assertions fail
Functional: healthy scope A closes with exit 0 while scope B is irreconcilable
Functional: an explicit global prepare with no --kyro-scope still reports B as a blocker
The gate runs inside npm run check, which passes end to end (exit 0)

checked_criteria: The gate fails when a startup surface drops --kyro-scope.
The gate fails when trace merge is not chronological.
The gate runs inside npm run check.
A healthy scope closes while an unrelated scope is irreconcilable.
An explicit global scan still reports the broken scope.

definitionOfDone: All four startup surfaces resolve the scope before integrity prepare and pass --kyro-scope through prepare, apply and post-repair doctor.
A healthy scope closes and passes scoped Doctor while an unrelated scope on disk is irreconcilable.
An explicit global scan without --kyro-scope still reports the broken scope.
No trace write can create a directory that scope discovery classifies as a scope, and leftover trace-only directories are ignored.
Previous-location trace history stays readable and merges by timestamp with a stable tie-break.
check:blast-radius-isolation runs in npm run check and fails when the contract regresses.
npm run check passes end to end and scoped Doctor passes.
